ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because Full turns Hares into copies of whatever off-tribe engine they stand beside, and the Moon-Scour then doubles the borrowed numbers, so every board asks a new placement puzzle.
ratings_why.distinct: A public moon you bend with Scryer, Watcher and Waxwell plays unlike today's tribes, though a phase cycle is the seed's obvious reading.

verdict_why: The engine is great; The Three Hares and stacked copies of The Hare in the Moon need wording a player can read.

points.text: The Three Hares is unclear: 'touching' is a whole chain in Bramble, so it's not clear which two units are 'the others of the three'. Name them, e.g. the two units touching it on the zigzag.
Say whether two Hare in the Moon effects stack (a Changeling at Full can copy one): twice twice is four, or still twice?

Changeling Sister needs a neighbour while Leveret in the Form wants none; that tension is good. A Full-only Changeling copying Dame Waxwell or Suitor Jack in the Recruit Phase is a lovely hidden line worth stating in the rules.

Keep Mother Meikle Care overshooting to Waning with The Hare in the Moon rather than fixing it to 'Turn to Full': it rewards the player who uses it on purpose to reach Waning payouts from the Charmer and Dusk Doe.
Jill Longshanks chaining Boxes is the ring build's heart; a Changeling or Silverpenny borrowing her text makes a second chain boxer, which is the kind of overlap to keep.

standouts.why: Changeling Sister makes every off-tribe engine a Hare card at Full; placement becomes the game.
The Moon-Scour doubling numbers in borrowed text reaches far past what the designer listed.
Dame Waxwell's turn, double-turn or hold is a real decision every turn.

weakest.why: Spring Jill is a plain body three turns in four.
Equinox Watcher pays only after a hold and fights Waxwell for the same lever.
Dew-Pond Scryer is a one-shot turn on a vanilla body.

flags.note: With golden Waxwell and golden Mad March Hare the stat output goes far past the golden ceiling, as the designer notes.
Longshanks can clear a weak board at Start of Combat before it attacks, and grows each win.
Which units count as 'the three' isn't readable.
Silverpenny copying an enemy capstone swings wildly by matchup.
